vulnerabilities.title: OOB_SIGNEDNESS_MISMATCH_IN_INDEX_CHECK

root_cause.description: edit_cookie 和 read_cookie 通过 scanf("%llu") 读入 unsigned long long 类型的索引 idx，但边界检查使用 jl（有符号小于）指令比较 idx 与 cookie_num。当用户输入一个 >= 0x8000000000000000 的无符号值时（如 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF = 18446744073709551615），该值在有符号比较中被解释为负数（-1），-1 < cookie_num 为真，通过检查。随后该极大无符号值被直接用于计算 msg[idx] 和 msg_size[idx] 的数组偏移（lea rdx,[rax*8] 和 lea rdx,[rax*4]），导致越界访问 .bss 中 msg 数组之后的内存区域。

No lower-bound check exists, but for unsigned input the lower bound is implicitly 0 — the real defect is the signed comparison allowing huge unsigned values to bypass the upper bound.

impact.reason: In read_cookie, the OOB msg[idx] dereference reads a pointer from beyond the msg array and printf("%s", ...) prints the content at that pointer. In edit_cookie, OOB msg_size[idx] is read to determine write length. The .bss layout after msg (msg_size at 0x4160, urandom at 0x41e0, cookie_num at 0x41e8) means specific OOB indices read these global values as pointers or sizes.

In edit_cookie, the OOB msg[idx] dereference reads a pointer from beyond the msg array, and read(0, msg[idx], msg_size[idx]-1) writes attacker-controlled data to whatever address that OOB pointer value points to. The OOB msg_size[idx] value controls the write length.
If the OOB-read pointer value from msg[idx] is an invalid address, dereferencing it (for read in read_cookie or write in edit_cookie) causes SIGSEGV.

evidence.description: cmp rdx,rax / jl 0x1692 — rdx holds idx from scanf("%llu") (unsigned long long), rax holds cookie_num. jl is signed less-than; values >= 0x8000000000000000 are treated as negative and pass the check.

mov rax,[rbp-0x10] (idx); lea rdx,[rax*4] + msg_size base -> OOB read msg_size[idx]; sub eax,0x1; movsxd rdx,eax; lea rcx,[rax*8] + msg base -> OOB read msg[idx]; read(0, msg[idx], msg_size[idx]-1) writes to OOB-dereferenced pointer.
cmp rdx,rax / jl 0x17bb — same signedness mismatch as edit_cookie; unsigned idx checked with signed jl.
mov rax,[rbp-0x10] (idx); lea rdx,[rax*8] + msg base -> OOB read msg[idx]; printf("%s", msg[idx]) prints content at OOB-dereferenced pointer.

msg array at 0x4060 (32 elements, 256 bytes), msg_size at 0x4160 (32 elements, 128 bytes), urandom at 0x41e0, cookie_num at 0x41e8. An idx value like 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE computes offset 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 from msg base, wrapping around address space. Smaller OOB indices (e.g. 32-63) access msg_size, urandom, cookie_num as if they were msg elements.

Dynamic verification: confirm the OOB msg[idx] dereference reads a controllable or interesting pointer value from .bss beyond msg
Dynamic verification: confirm read(0, OOB_ptr, OOB_size) actually writes to the dereferenced address

vulnerabilities.title: HEAP_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_VIA_ZERO_SIZE_INTEGER_UNDERFLOW

root_cause.description: create_cookie 允许 size=0 通过检查（cmp rax,0x100 / jle — 0 <= 256 为真），calloc(0,1) 成功返回一个最小堆块（glibc 中为 0x20 字节的 chunk），msg_size[cookie_num] 存储 0（int 类型）。当后续 edit_cookie 对该 cookie 执行编辑时，计算写入长度为 msg_size[idx]-1 = 0-1 = -1（int 算术），然后 movsxd rdx,eax 将 -1 符号扩展为 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF（64 位），作为 read() 的 count 参数。read(0, msg[idx], 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) 尝试从 stdin 读取极大数量的字节写入一个极小的堆块，导致堆缓冲区溢出。

attack_surface.input: size=0 via scanf("%lld") in create_cookie; then message data via read(0,...) in edit_cookie
attack_surface.entry_function: main -> create_cookie (create with size=0) -> edit_cookie (edit the zero-size cookie)
data_flow: create_cookie: scanf("%lld", &size) reads 0 into [rbp-0x18]
create_cookie: cmp rax,0x100 / jle — 0 <= 256 passes check
create_cookie: calloc(0,1) returns minimal heap chunk (0x20 bytes in glibc)
create_cookie: msg_size[cookie_num] = (int)0 — stored as 4-byte int 0
edit_cookie: eax = msg_size[idx] = 0 (int)
edit_cookie: sub eax,0x1 -> eax = 0xFFFFFFFF (int -1)
edit_cookie: movsxd rdx,eax -> rdx = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF (size_t)
edit_cookie: read(0, msg[idx], 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) — heap buffer overflow

security_check.expected: create_cookie should reject size=0 (minimum size of 1) or edit_cookie should check msg_size[idx] > 0 before computing msg_size[idx]-1.
security_check.actual: create_cookie checks size <= 0x100 with jle (signed), allowing 0. edit_cookie computes msg_size[idx]-1 without checking for zero, and sign-extends the result to 64-bit for read()'s count parameter.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: No lower-bound check on size (size >= 1) in create_cookie. No zero-check on msg_size[idx] before subtraction in edit_cookie. The int-to-size_t sign extension via movsxd converts -1 to 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF.

vulnerable_operation.operation: read() with enormous count into small heap buffer
vulnerable_operation.address: 0x16b9-0x16de (edit_cookie: sub eax,0x1; movsxd rdx,eax; read(0, msg[idx], rdx))
vulnerable_operation.target: heap chunk from calloc(0,1) — minimal size (0x20 bytes in glibc 2.39)
vulnerable_operation.size: 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF (effectively unlimited) bytes written to ~0x20 byte heap chunk

impact.reason: read() writes attacker-controlled data from stdin far beyond the bounds of the small heap chunk allocated by calloc(0,1), corrupting adjacent heap metadata and heap objects.
The overflow overwrites heap chunk metadata (size, prev_size, fd/bk pointers) and adjacent heap objects, corrupting heap state.
Heap metadata corruption from the overflow will likely cause a crash on subsequent heap operations (malloc/free).

evidence.description: mov rax,[rbp-0x18] (size); cmp rax,0x100; jle 0x140a — signed comparison, size=0 passes (0 <= 256).
mov rax,[rbp-0x18] (size=0); mov esi,0x1; mov rdi,rax; call calloc — calloc(0,1) returns minimal heap chunk.
mov rdx,[rbp-0x18] (size=0); mov ecx,edx (truncates to int 0); mov DWORD PTR [rdx+rax*1],ecx — msg_size[cookie_num] = 0 (int).
mov eax,DWORD PTR [rdx+rax*1] (msg_size[idx]=0); sub eax,0x1 (eax=0xFFFFFFFF); movsxd rdx,eax (rdx=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF); read(0, msg[idx], rdx) — heap overflow with unlimited write length.

verification_required: Dynamic verification: create a cookie with size=0, then edit it and confirm read() receives count=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
Dynamic verification: confirm the overflow corrupts adjacent heap chunks
Dynamic verification: confirm calloc(0,1) returns a usable pointer (not NULL) under glibc 2.39

vulnerabilities.title: NULL_POINTER_DEREFERENCE_VIA_NEGATIVE_CALLOC_SIZE

root_cause.description: create_cookie 通过 scanf("%lld") 读入 long long 类型的 size，检查使用 cmp rax,0x100 / jle（有符号小于等于）。负数（如 -1）满足 -1 <= 256，通过检查。随后 calloc(size, 1) 被调用，其中 size 为负数；calloc 的参数为 size_t（无符号），-1 被转换为 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF，这是一个极大的分配请求，calloc 会失败并返回 NULL。返回的 NULL 指针被直接用于后续的 read(0, NULL, size) 调用和 NUL 终止操作，没有 NULL 检查，导致 NULL 指针解引用。

data_flow: scanf("%lld", &size) reads negative value (e.g. -1) into [rbp-0x18]
cmp rax,0x100 / jle — signed comparison, -1 <= 256 passes
calloc(-1, 1) — size_t conversion: -1 -> 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, allocation fails, returns NULL
NULL stored in [rbp-0x10]
read(0, NULL, -1) — buf is NULL
mov rax,[rbp-0x10] (NULL); add rax,rdx; movzx eax,BYTE PTR [rax] — NULL dereference

security_check.expected: create_cookie should reject size <= 0 (check size > 0 && size <= 0x100) and/or check calloc return value for NULL.
security_check.actual: Only checks size <= 0x100 with signed jle, allowing negative values. No NULL check on calloc return value.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: No lower-bound check (size > 0). No NULL check on calloc return value before use in read() and NUL-termination.

vulnerable_operation.operation: NULL pointer dereference via unchecked calloc failure
vulnerable_operation.address: 0x1451-0x1458 (mov rax,[rbp-0x10]=NULL; add rax,rdx; movzx eax,BYTE PTR [rax])

impact.reason: calloc returns NULL for the impossible allocation size, and the NULL pointer is dereferenced when checking the last byte for newline (movzx eax,BYTE PTR [rax] where rax=NULL+read_ret).
Dereferencing the NULL-derived address causes SIGSEGV, crashing the program.

evidence.description: cmp rax,0x100 / jle — signed comparison allows negative size values (e.g. -1 <= 256).
call calloc@plt; mov QWORD PTR [rbp-0x10],rax — calloc return value stored without NULL check.
mov eax,DWORD PTR [rbp-0x1c] (read return); movsxd rdx,eax; mov rax,QWORD PTR [rbp-0x10] (NULL); add rax,rdx; movzx eax,BYTE PTR [rax] — dereferences NULL+read_ret, SIGSEGV.

verification_required: Dynamic verification: input -1 as size in create_cookie and confirm calloc returns NULL
Dynamic verification: confirm the NULL dereference causes SIGSEGV at the NUL-termination check

vulnerabilities.title: USE_AFTER_FREE_DANGLING_POINTER_IN_EAT_COOKIE

root_cause.description: eat_cookie 使用 remove-from-array 模式：free(msg[idx]) 后执行 msg[idx]=msg[cookie_num-1] 和 msg_size[idx]=msg_size[cookie_num-1]，然后 cookie_num--。当随机选中的 idx == cookie_num-1 时，free(msg[idx]) 释放了堆块，但 msg[idx]=msg[cookie_num-1] 是将 msg[idx] 自身的值（已 free 的指针，因为 free 不清除指针值）写回 msg[idx]，导致 msg[idx] 仍然保存着已释放的堆指针。虽然 cookie_num-- 使该索引在逻辑上不可达（idx == 新的 cookie_num），但物理上悬垂指针仍存在于 .bss 的 msg 数组中。此外，当 idx != cookie_num-1 时，move 操作将 msg[cookie_num-1] 的指针复制到 msg[idx]，但 msg[cookie_num-1] 位置未被清零，造成两个槽位指向同一堆块（指针别名），后续操作可能通过其中一个槽位 free 后，另一个槽位仍保存已 free 指针。

attack_surface.input: random index from /dev/urandom (urandom_byte % cookie_num) — not directly attacker-controlled
data_flow: fread(&buf, 1, 1, urandom) — read 1 random byte
idx = buf % cookie_num — random index selection
printf("%s", msg[idx]) — print cookie content before free
free(msg[idx]) — release heap block
msg[idx] = msg[cookie_num-1] — move last pointer into freed slot
msg_size[idx] = msg_size[cookie_num-1] — move last size into freed slot
cookie_num-- — decrement count
When idx == cookie_num-1: msg[idx] = msg[idx] (self-assignment of freed pointer), dangling pointer remains in msg[idx]

security_check.expected: After free(msg[idx]), the freed slot should be set to NULL (msg[idx] = NULL) or the move operation should clear the source slot (msg[cookie_num-1] = NULL).
security_check.actual: No NULL-ification of freed pointers. When idx == cookie_num-1, the freed pointer is written back into the same slot. When idx != cookie_num-1, the source slot (msg[cookie_num-1]) retains the duplicated pointer value without clearing.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: No pointer invalidation after free. The move-last-into-hole pattern does not clear the source slot, leaving dangling pointers in .bss.

vulnerable_operation.operation: free(msg[idx]) followed by dangling pointer retention in msg array
vulnerable_operation.expression: free(msg[idx]); msg[idx] = msg[cookie_num-1]; // when idx==cookie_num-1, self-assignment of freed pointer

impact.reason: After free, the heap chunk's content may be overwritten by glibc's free-list management (fd/bk pointers). If the dangling pointer is later dereferenced (via edit_cookie or read_cookie when the index becomes reachable again), the program reads/writes freed heap memory that now contains allocator metadata.

If the dangling pointer becomes reachable again (e.g. through create_cookie reusing the slot index without overwriting, or through the OOB signedness bug accessing beyond cookie_num), edit_cookie would write to freed heap memory, corrupting allocator metadata.

eat_cookie prints printf("%s", msg[idx]) before free. If prior frees have placed heap chunks into unsorted bin (for larger sizes), the freed chunk's fd/bk pointers contain libc/heap addresses. If a dangling pointer is later read via read_cookie, these addresses would be leaked.

evidence.description: call free@plt (free msg[idx]); then mov rax,[rip+cookie_num-1]; lea rcx,[rax*8]; lea rax,[rip+msg]; mov rax,[rcx+rax] (read msg[cookie_num-1]); movsxd rdx,edx(idx); lea rcx,[rdx*8]; lea rdx,[rip+msg]; mov [rcx+rdx],rax (msg[idx]=msg[cookie_num-1]). When idx==cookie_num-1, this is self-assignment of the freed pointer.

The move-last pattern does not clear msg[cookie_num-1] after copying to msg[idx]. When idx != cookie_num-1, both msg[idx] and msg[cookie_num-1] point to the same heap block. If one is later freed (via another eat_cookie), the other becomes a dangling pointer. However, cookie_num-- makes msg[cookie_num-1] (old) unreachable through normal index checks.

printf("%s", msg[idx]) is called BEFORE free(msg[idx]). This prints heap content that may contain libc/heap addresses if the chunk was previously freed and reallocated (from unsorted bin). The index is random, not attacker-controlled, limiting exploitability of this specific leak.

verification_required: Dynamic verification: confirm that when idx==cookie_num-1, msg[idx] retains the freed pointer value after eat_cookie returns
Dynamic verification: determine if the dangling pointer can be made reachable through a sequence of eat/create operations or through the BUG-001 signedness mismatch
Dynamic verification: confirm whether create_cookie always overwrites the dangling slot before it can be accessed via edit/read
